name: Movement in and out of cells

questions.q: What is the process called when particles move from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration down a concentration gradient?
Which term describes the net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential through a partially permeable membrane?
What mechanism do cells use to move substances against a concentration gradient, requiring energy from respiration?
What happens to a plant cell when it is placed in pure water and takes in water until its cell wall resists further expansion?
Which factor increases the rate of diffusion across a cell membrane?
What term describes an animal cell that has shrivelled up after losing water in a concentrated salt solution?
What is the main function of root hair cells in relation to transport?
a: To absorb water and mineral ions from the soil efficiently
To transport sugars down the stem

questions.q: Why is the surface area to volume ratio critically important for single-celled organisms?
a: It allows complex organs to form inside
It speeds up internal body temperature
It allows efficient exchange of substances by diffusion alone

questions.q: What happens to a red blood cell when placed into a solution with a much higher water potential (pure water)?
a: It develops a rigid cell wall

questions.q: What property of cell membranes allows small molecules like water and oxygen to pass through while blocking larger molecules?
Which of these substances typically moves into animal cells via simple diffusion during cellular respiration?
What term is used to describe plant cells that have lost water by osmosis, causing the cell membrane to pull away from the cell wall?
How do mineral ions like nitrates usually enter plant root hair cells from the soil when soil concentration is lower than inside the root?
What effect does increasing temperature have on the rate of diffusion?
a: It slows diffusion down to zero
It increases particle kinetic energy, speeding up the rate of diffusion
It has no effect on particle movement

questions.q: What is the term for the state of a plant tissue when cells are soft and limp because water has left the vacuole?
Which structure in a plant cell prevents it from bursting when placed in pure distilled water?
Why do active transport mechanisms in cell membranes require cellular energy (ATP)?
a: Because particles are moving against their concentration gradient
Because it cools down the cell
Because water molecules are too heavy

questions.q: What role do carrier proteins play in cell membranes?
a: They bind to specific molecules and change shape to move them across the membrane

questions.q: Which of the following processes is entirely passive and does not require energy from respiration?
What happens to the rate of diffusion if the distance across which particles must travel increases?
Which term describes the movement of dissolved sugars and amino acids through phloem tissue?
What is the physical state of water potential in pure water compared to a concentrated sugar solution?
In a diffusion experiment using Visking tubing filled with starch solution in a beaker of iodine, why does iodine move inside?
a: Starch molecules are too small and move out
Iodine molecules are small enough to pass through the partially permeable pores

questions.q: What is the primary reason multicellular organisms require specialized transport systems (like blood vessels or xylem)?
a: To overcome long distances where simple diffusion is too slow

questions.q: How does an increase in the concentration gradient affect the rate of osmosis?
a: It increases the net movement of water down the gradient
It reverses the direction of water flow
It has no effect on water movement

questions.q: Which cell component provides the energy required for active transport processes in living cells?
What occurs when the concentration of solutes outside a cell equals the concentration inside the cell (isotonic condition)?
Which of these molecules is too large to pass through a standard partially permeable cell membrane without specialized transport proteins?
What term describes the net movement of particles through protein channels down a concentration gradient without energy input?
Why do plant roots wilt when excessive chemical fertilizer is added to surrounding dry soil?
a: Soil water potential becomes higher than root cell water potential
Soil water potential becomes lower, causing water to leave root cells by osmosis
Fertilizer dissolves root cell walls instantly

questions.q: What is the primary driving force behind water movement up a plant stem during transpiration?
a: Evaporation of water from mesophyll cell surfaces into air spaces

questions.q: Which factor decreases the efficiency of gas exchange across an alveolar or cell membrane?
a: Increased thickness of the barrier membrane

questions.q: What happens to red blood cells when placed in a hypertonic (concentrated) salt solution?
a: They shrink and become crenated as water leaves by osmosis

questions.q: What is the relationship between surface area and volume as an organism grows larger?
a: Surface area increases faster than volume
Surface area to volume ratio decreases
Surface area and volume remain equal
